headline: AI rout goes global on OpEx Friday — Anthropic's debut couldn't stop a six-session skid, Waller's half-point threat is live, and chips are down from Tokyo to Frankfurt before the open

Anthropic's record debut flipped sell-the-news as AMD's China shock and healthcare's regulatory spiral extended the S&P 500's longest losing streak since 2024 — OPEX Friday arrives in a negative-gamma, hawkish-Fed crosswind
Nvidia's beat couldn't hold the gap — a leaderless AI giant, hawkish Fed minutes, and the Anthropic IPO pricing make Thursday's open a true two-way event

A four-part storm — US chip-export curbs hitting Asian supply chains, Nvidia's first post-Jensen Huang earnings report looming after the bell, a reported NSANet outage spooking infrastructure sentiment, and a hawkish Fed official piling on after a retail-sales beat — sent all four major US indices sharply lower into the afternoon.
AI chips, a leaderless Nvidia, and a new export rule sent tech to the session's worst losses — Tuesday's Nvidia earnings are now the week's defining binary for every index.
